Closed-loop MPC simulation

Source: R/mpc.R
ctrl_simulate_mpc.Rd

Run the receding-horizon loop: at each sample, measure (or estimate) the state, solve the MPC problem, apply the first input to the plant and advance. The simulation plant may differ from the prediction model (model mismatch) and may include input disturbances and measurement noise.

Usage

ctrl_simulate_mpc(
  mpc,
  x0,
  steps,
  reference = NULL,
  plant = NULL,
  disturbance = NULL,
  noise = NULL,
  estimator = NULL,
  u0 = NULL,
  on_failure = c("stop", "hold", "shifted"),
  warm_start = TRUE
)

Arguments

mpc

A ctrl_mpc object.

x0

Initial plant state.

steps

Number of samples.

reference

List with x, u and/or y references (see ctrl_mpc_qp()); with an estimator, y is the output setpoint.

plant

Simulation plant (default: the prediction model).

disturbance

Input disturbance added to the plant input: a vector with one value per input (constant), a matrix with one row per sample, or a function of the sample index. For a single input, a vector with one value per sample is also accepted. The plant sees the effective input \(u_k + d_k\) in both \(x_{k+1} = A x_k + B(u_k + d_k)\) and \(y_k = C x_k + D(u_k + d_k)\). The measurement used to compute \(u_k\) is taken before \(u_k\) is applied, so it sees the input and disturbance held over the previous sample (zero before the first).

noise

Measurement noise on the outputs (same formats).

estimator

Optional ctrl_mpc_estimator for output feedback with offset-free tracking; without it the true state is measured.

u0

Input applied before the first sample (for rate constraints).

on_failure

"stop", "hold" or "shifted".

warm_start

Warm start each solve with the shifted previous plan.

Value

An object of class ctrl_mpc_simulation with time, x (true states, (steps+1) x n), y, u, xhat, dhat, a log data frame (status, iterations, solve time, objective, max violation, fallback) and summary counts.

Details

Failure handling. If a QP solve fails, on_failure decides what happens; the choice is always recorded in the fallback column: "stop" (default) raises an error with the solver status, "hold" applies the previous input (clipped to the input bounds) and "shifted" applies the next move of the last successful plan (then holds its last move). No input is ever applied silently.

Examples

plant <- ctrl_c2d(ctrl_ss(matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE), c(0, 1),
                          c(1, 0)), 0.1)
mpc <- ctrl_mpc(plant, horizon = 20, Q = diag(c(10, 1)), R = 0.1,
                u_min = -1, u_max = 1, x_min = c(-Inf, -0.6),
                x_max = c(Inf, 0.6))
sim <- ctrl_simulate_mpc(mpc, x0 = c(2, 0), steps = 80)
summary(sim)
#> MPC simulation: 80 samples, 0 failed solves (0%)
#>   solver statuses: solved = 80
#>   solve time: mean 0.000649 s, max 0.00187 s; mean iterations 406.6
#>   max input bound violation: 9.43e-11
#>   max state bound violation (true plant): 0
#>   max slack: 0
